# 15 Trem Chop — voicing round (Batch 3B, the wreck and chop set)

*Generated by tests/voicing/batch03b.py. Level reading: RMS over the note-on region of the chop phrase (phrase o), off parts of the chop included; matched to the bank reference (-18.0 dBFS RMS) by VOLUME; phrase (b)'s reading is in the table too. Every change is before -> after under the echo rule. WAVs are on the listen/batch-03b-chapter1-wreck-and-chop branch only.*

**Recommended: B centre** - MONO: two bright saws 3.9 cents apart, both oscillators at LEVEL 127, the 24 dB low-pass open (CUTOFF 95, DRIVE 60), amp SUSTAIN 127, no delay (the original's 1/8 delay at MIX 30 is removed: a choice to keep the chop dry; on a held note it changed the depth by 0.1 dB in a trial render). THE CHOP: the LFO is a SQUARE at RATE 101 = 8.10 Hz, AMP 127 (the amp law is `1 - AMP/256 x (1 - lfo)`: full level for the high half, 1/128 = -42 dB for the low half, never exactly silent). Measured on the held A3: rate 8.10 Hz, on -15.4 / off -58.1 dBFS, depth 42.8 dB, on 52 % of the cycle; the edge rises 10-90 % in 0.77 ms on an A6 probe (the reading is limited by its one-period window, 0.57 ms; the engine's own amp ramp across a 16-sample block is 0.36 ms): a hard gate, not a tremolo. LFO PITCH was 8, inert (the law is (d*d)>>7 = 0 below 12); it is now 0 (the first real value, 12, would put a square +-9 cent pitch step on every edge; untested). LFO PHASE SYNC: every detached note starts the chop ON (phrase p: 8 of 8 notes start ON, the first edge at 59 ms +-2.2 after the note-on); a legato note in MONO slides without restarting it. **The wavering:** the edge timing is tidy: s.d. of the rising edges about a straight line 0.16 ms (the reading's resolution is 0.5 ms), the period s.d. 0.25 ms, and VINTAGE does not move it (0 / 60 / 127: 0.18 / 0.24 / 0.16 ms in the VINTAGE probe): VINTAGE 60 wanders the pitch and cutoff, not the LFO. What does waver the edges is in the other variants: C lets the chop free-run (0 of 8 notes start ON at this rate and phase, the first edge slides 46 -> 24 ms over the phrase), D puts the two voices of each note an eighth of a cycle apart (rise 16.3 ms; the held note spends 35 % of the time off, 31 % at one voice's level, 33 % at full, B: 49 / 1 / 50 %). Level -18.0 dBFS on the chop phrase (off parts included), -16.6 on phrase (b), peak -10.5, crest 7.5 dB, centroid 1958 Hz; worst case 1366 host instr/sample (the original 1402).

## What to listen to

`*_chop.wav` is the one to judge (a 2.4 s held A3, a six-note riff of long notes, the chord A3+E4+A4: a MONO patch plays its last note, D plays all three), `*_chopshort.wav` has eight 110 ms notes and four 240 ms notes (the chop against the gate), `*_riff.wav` / `*_stabs.wav` / `*_held.wav` are the pilot phrases.
Listen for: how hard the edges are (B), whether C's free-running chop (a note can start in an off part) is broken or just unreliable, and whether D's two-voice smear is a stutter or a mush.

*Notes.* Chop figures are read on the held A3 (3.3-5.3 s of phrase o) from a 2 ms RMS envelope: ON = the median of the upper half, OFF = the median of the lowest tenth, depth = ON - OFF; edges = the midpoint crossings. **Tempo:** the LFO has NO tempo sync: its rate is the RATE knob alone (`0.05 x 600^(RATE/127)` Hz, a step is about 5 %). The tempo (GLOBAL page, a MIDI clock, REC tap on the BBD page) drives the arp, the delay's SYNC and ALLEY, never the LFO. Nearest RATE bytes
(cycles per second; one cycle = one on and one off): 90 BPM quarter / eighth / sixteenth = 1.5 / 3.0 / 6.0 Hz = RATE 68 (1.54) / 81 (2.96) / 95 (5.99); 120 BPM = 2.0 / 4.0 / 8.0 Hz = RATE 73 (1.98) / 87 (4.00) / 101 (8.10); 140 BPM = 2.33 / 4.67 / 9.33 Hz = RATE 76 (2.30) / 90 (4.65) / 104 (9.42). A byte can be up to 2.5 % off the tempo, so a free-running chop slides against a long phrase (8.10 Hz against 120 BPM eighths drifts 3 ms a step; the phrase p
reading with LFO PHASE FREE shows it). The nearest thing to a lock the existing controls give is LFO PHASE SYNC (the first key of a detached note restarts the LFO, so the chop is aligned to each note, not to the beat). **A free chop at a tempo-matched rate can start every note OFF** (C, phrase p at 120 BPM: all eight notes begin in an off part and the first edge slides 46 -> 24 ms; where it starts depends on where the free-running LFO happens to be): the reason B is SYNC. LFO DELAY would fade the chop in (untested here).
The shape options (all one shared LFO): SQUARE = the hard on/off used; RAMP / SAW = one hard edge and one linear ramp per cycle (a rising or falling swell; untested here); S&H = a random level at each step; TRI = the gentle tremolo not wanted; RANDOM = a smooth wander. Only SQUARE was rendered in the variants; the others are read from the LFO code (`lfo_shape`) and **untested here**.
